id: fpbs-pu-nonuniqueness-commuting-subgroups
kind: claim
title: Groups generated by two commuting infinite subgroups have no unique infinite cluster at p_u
---

**ESTABLISHED (imported).** Let `G` be a nonamenable group generated by two
commuting infinite finitely generated subgroups `H` and `K`. Then for every
Cayley graph of `G`, Bernoulli bond percolation at `p = p_u` does not have a
unique infinite cluster.

Gaboriau--Tucker-Drob, arXiv:1509.00247v1, Theorem 2.1 (read from source
2026-09-11). It covers every direct product of a nonamenable and an infinite
group under every generating set (Hutchcroft--Pan, arXiv:2409.12283v1, Theorem
1.14, restate this as "obstacle to uniqueness"). It also covers every
nonamenable group with an infinite finitely generated center, taking `H` to be
the center.

This is the **weak** conclusion `N_infinity(p_u) in {0, +infinity}`
(Hutchcroft--Pan Definition 1.11 states the dichotomy explicitly). By
`fpbs-pu-nonuniqueness-cannot-separate` it does not imply `p_c < p_u`.

Status records an imported theorem, not independent mathematical verification.
